deliverable: fake/fake_apple.c: a Linux implementation of EVERY function and constant declared in include/n2_apple.h, compiled with -DN2_HOST_FAKE. Objects are reference counted structs with a type tag; CFRelease at count 0 frees; a global live-object counter `long n2fake_live_objects(void)` lets tests assert no leak. n2fake_cfstr interns. CFDictionary: insertion-ordered array of (key,value), keys compared with CFEqual (strings by content, numbers by value, others by pointer), retains keys and values. CFArray likewise. CFNumber stores int64 or double per type. CMBlockBuffer: owned malloc block (memoryBlock NULL + AssureMemoryNow) or a borrowed block; Replace/Copy bounds-checked (-12704 on out of range). CMSampleBufferCreateReady keeps block buffer, format description, timing[0], sizes; attachments array created on demand with one mutable dictionary per sample. CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromH264ParameterSets copies the parameter sets (rejects count < 2, NAL header length not 1/2/4, first set's nal_unit_type != 7: -12712) and ...GetH264ParameterSetAtIndex returns them. CVPixelBuffer: CVPixelBufferCreate for N2_PIXFMT_420V/420F (two planes, stride = width rounded up to 64) and N2_PIXFMT_I420; Lock/Unlock counted (GetBaseAddressOfPlane while unlocked returns NULL so that missing locks are caught).

fake/fake_vt.c + fake_apple.h: the VideoToolbox side of include/n2vt_abi.h. CMDerivedObjectCreate(alloc, vtable, classID, out): allocates object + baseClass->derivedStorageSize zeroed bytes, stores the vtable (as n2_VTVideoEncoderVTable); CMBaseObjectGetDerivedStorage; VTVideoEncoderGetClassID returns a fixed id (creation with another id fails -12780); VTVideoEncoderGetCMBaseObject is the identity; releasing the object calls baseClass->finalize. VTRegisterVideoEncoder[WithInfo] append to a registry readable by tests: `int n2fake_vt_registered(int index, uint32_t *codec, CFDictionaryRef *info, n2_VTVideoEncoderCreateInstance *fn)` and `void n2fake_vt_reset(void)`. A fake session for driving an encoder the way VideoToolbox does: `struct n2fake_session *n2fake_session_create(n2_VTVideoEncoderCreateInstance fn, uint32_t codec, int width, int height)` (calls fn then encoderClass->startSession with the session token), `OSStatus n2fake_session_encode(s, CVPixelBufferRef, CMTime pts, CMTime duration, CFDictionaryRef frameProps)` (calls encodeFrame with a fresh frame token), `OSStatus n2fake_session_complete(s)`, `OSStatus n2fake_session_set_property(s, key, value)` / `copy_property` (through baseClass), `int n2fake_session_emitted(s, int index, OSStatus *status, uint32_t *flags, CMSampleBufferRef *sbuf, void **frameToken)`, `CFDictionaryRef n2fake_session_pixel_attributes(s)` (what the encoder passed to VTEncoderSessionSetPixelBufferAttributes), `void n2fake_session_destroy(s)`. VTEncoderSessionEmitEncodedFrame records (retaining the sample buffer) and asserts the frame token is one that was submitted and not yet emitted; a second emit for the same token, or an emit for an unknown token, sets a sticky `n2fake_session_protocol_errors(s)` counter.
The fake is strict on purpose: NULL where real CF would crash -> abort() with a message naming the function (tests of error paths use the documented NULL-safe calls only).

Tables typed in from the Recommendation as {length, bits} pairs; a self-check at start-up of the test verifies each table is a prefix-free code.

n2avc_intra.c: Intra16x16 prediction modes Vertical, Horizontal, DC (all availability cases, clause 8.3.3) and Plane; chroma DC (8.3.4, per 4x4 block rules), Horizontal, Vertical, Plane. Mode choice: least SAD among the available modes. mb_type for I slices = 1 + pred_mode + 4*chroma_cbp_class + (luma AC present ? 12 : 0) (table 7-11), +5 in P slices. I_PCM (mb_type 25 / 30) as the fallback when a macroblock's bits would exceed 3200 or the slice buffer runs short.

n2avc_mb.c: n2avc_flush_skip_run, n2avc_inter_residual, n2avc_write_inter_residual, n2avc_intra_mb, n2avc_cbp_inter_code (table 9-4 column 'Inter' for ChromaArrayType 1/2) exactly as declared in n2avc_int.h.

n2avc_enc.c: n2avc_open/headers/encode/reconfigure/reconstruction/close of n2avc.h. All memory allocated in open (frames with N2AVC_PAD borders, mbinfo, per-slice RBSP buffers of 1.5 x raw size + 64 KiB, output buffer). Converts NV12/I420 input into the padded planar source. `threads` slices = equal bands of macroblock rows, coded by a persistent pthread pool (threads == 1: no thread created); slices are joined in order into the packet (AVCC lengths or Annex-B start codes). IDR when: first picture, force_idr, keyint reached, N2AVC_F_INTRA_ONLY. After each picture: extend the reconstruction's borders (replicate edge samples N2AVC_PAD luma / 16 chroma) and swap rec/ref. Calls n2avc_rc_* around each picture and n2avc_inter_slice_begin/end + n2avc_p_mb for P slices as n2avc_int.h says.

deliverable: vectors/gen_yuv.py (pure Python 3, no numpy, no Pillow needed): `gen_yuv.py --pattern {gradient,squares,pan,static,noise,text} --size WxH --frames N [--format i420|nv12] --out file.yuv`. Exact definitions (frame f, luma x,y): gradient: Y = (x + 2*y + 3*f) & 255, for chroma sample (cx, cy): Cb = 128 + ((cx + f) & 31), Cr = 128 - (cy & 31) (same as the probe's probe_fill_nv12 without the square); squares: gradient of frame 0 as a still background plus three 32x32 squares of luma 235/16/128 at (16+4f, 16+2f), (W-48-3f, 24+f), (W//2, H-48-2f) clipped; pan: a fixed 'world' picture world(x,y) = ((x*7) ^ (y*13) ^ ((x*y) >> 4)) & 255 sampled at (x+3f, y-2f+64); static: frame 0 of 'pan' repeated; noise: LCG state = state*1664525 + 1013904223 mod 2^32, seed 1 at the start of the file, one step per sample, value = state >> 24, order Y plane, Cb, Cr per frame; text: 8x8 cells, cell (cx,cy) is 16 or 235 by ((cx*31 + cy*17 + f//5) % 7 < 3), chroma 128. Writes row by row with bytearrays (a 1920x1080 frame must take < 3 s).

vectors/make_vectors.sh [quick|full]: generates into vectors/data/ (git-ignored style: reproducible, deletable): raw sequences for the sizes of PLAN.md section 7 ('quick': 176x144, 178x146, 640x480 x 10 frames; 'full' adds 1280x720 x 10 and 1920x1080 and 1918x1078 x 4); golden compressed streams made with the installed tools from 'squares' 176x144, 8 frames: h264 Constrained Baseline (x264 --profile baseline --keyint 8 --bframes 0 --qp 28, Annex-B) and High with CABAC+B frames (for decoder tests), hevc (x265 --preset fast --qp 30 --keyint 8, no B frames: --bframes 0), jpeg (cjpeg -quality 85 of frame 0 converted to PPM by a helper in gen_yuv.py using BT.601 full-range integer maths defined in the script), heic (heif-enc of the same PPM), a 2-frame AV1 (aomenc --limit=2 --cpu-used=8, as IVF/OBU) ; and for each stream the DECODED pictures' md5 per frame via `ffmpeg -v error -i X -f framemd5 -pix_fmt yuv420p -` (stored in the manifest; for H.264/HEVC these are normative).

vectors/manifest.json: {"version":1, "raw":[{name, pattern, width, height, frames, format, path, sha256}], "streams":[{name, codec, profile, width, height, frames, path, sha256, made_with (exact command line + tool version string), frame_md5:[...], luma_md5_first_frame}]}. luma_md5_first_frame = md5 of the first decoded picture's luma, width bytes per row, no padding (what the probe computes).

vectors/make_embedded.py -> vectors/embedded_vectors.h: C arrays for the probe, total under 48 KiB of data: for h264 (baseline stream) and hevc: each parameter set as its own array WITHOUT start code (H.264: SPS, PPS; HEVC: VPS, SPS, PPS), each access unit converted from Annex-B to AVCC (4-byte big-endian length before each NAL, parameter-set and AUD NALs removed), `struct n2vec_frame { const uint8_t *data; unsigned size; unsigned keyframe; }` tables, width/height/frame count, and the golden luma md5 string of frame 0; the JPEG and the HEIC file as arrays with width/height. A static inline `n2vec_count()`; everything `static const` so that including it twice in different files is harmless.

vectors/check_vectors.sh: regenerates 'quick' into a temp dir and verifies every sha256 and md5 of the manifest (determinism), and that the whole vectors/ directory is under 40 MB (`du -sb`). Last line 'N2TEST WP09 PASS n/n'.

oracle/check_h264.py --stream out.264 [--recon recon.yuv] [--source src.yuv] --size WxH --frames N [--stats stats.json] [--expect key=value ...]: (a) `ffmpeg -v error -i out.264 -f rawvideo -pix_fmt yuv420p` must exit 0 with EMPTY stderr and give exactly N frames of WxH; (b) with --recon: byte-identical, else print the first differing (frame, plane, x, y, macroblock address = (y//16)*mb_w + x//16) and fail; (c) with --source: luma PSNR per frame >= a floor by QP from stats.json (QP<=12: 44 dB, <=26: 36, <=32: 32, <=40: 27, else 22) ; (d) headers through `ffmpeg -v error -i out.264 -c copy -bsf:v trace_headers -f null - 2>&1` parsed for: profile_idc 66, constraint_set0_flag 1, constraint_set1_flag 1, level_idc per the table of n2avc.h, pic_order_cnt_type 2, max_num_ref_frames 1, frame_mbs_only_flag 1, entropy_coding_mode_flag 0, frame cropping equal to the expected offsets for WxH, max_num_reorder_frames 0, and slice count per picture == threads when given via --expect slices=T; nal_unit_type sequence starts with 7, 8, 5; (e) an independent Annex-B scanner written in the script checks that no 00 00 00/01/02 sequence occurs inside a NAL payload and counts NALs. Exit 0 and last line 'ORACLE h264 PASS ...' or exit 1 with the reason.

oracle/run_oracle.sh h264 [quick|full]: for the matrix {sizes of WP09's quick/full set} x {gradient, squares, pan, static, noise} x QP {10, 26, 40, 51} and bitrate {300k, 2M} x threads {1, 4} x {intra-only, P}: gen_yuv.py -> build/WP03/n2avc_cli (built by WP03's run_tests.sh; rebuilt here from avc/*.c with -O2 and ASan if missing) -> check_h264.py; plus AVCC mode converted to Annex-B by an independent converter in the script; prints one line per case and 'N2TEST WP10-h264 PASS n/n'. 'quick' must finish in under 90 s on one core; each case's temp files are deleted.

oracle/check_mp4.py file.mp4|.mov --expect-video avc1|hvc1 --size WxH --min-frames N [--audio aac]: via `ffprobe -v error -show_streams -show_format -of json` (codec_name, width, height, nb_frames or counted packets, duration, audio stream presence) AND an independent box walker in the script (ftyp, moov, mdat present; stsd entry type; avcC/hvcC present and its SPS parses to the same size) ; then full decode with ffmpeg must exit 0. For files pulled from the phone.

oracle/check_abi.py + abi_expect.json: generates a C file that prints sizeof/offsetof for every member of n2_CMBaseClass, n2_VTVideoEncoderClass, n2_VTVideoEncoderVTable, CMTime, CMSampleTimingInfo, compiles it for the host (LP64, same layout as arm64) with -DN2_HOST_FAKE, and compares with abi_expect.json whose numbers are typed in from PLAN.md section 1.3 / the comment block of n2vt_abi.h (e.g. VTVideoEncoderClass: startSession 0x08, encodeFrame 0x10, completeFrames 0x18, copySupportedPropertyDictionary 0x20, prepareToEncodeFrames 0x38, startTileSession 0x88, encodeTile 0x98, completeTiles 0xa0, size 0xa8; CMBaseClass: derivedStorageSize 0x08, finalize 0x20, copyDebugDescription 0x28, copyProperty 0x30, setProperty 0x38, size 0x58). Second mode `check_abi.py --dylib build/ios/Slim.videoencoder`: `llvm-nm -gU` shows exactly _SLIMEncoderRegister and _n2vt_version; `llvm-nm -u` symbols are all in sdk/lib/*.tbd; install name and arm64 slice as expected; no string containing '/home/' in the binary.

oracle/parse_probe.py probe-*.jsonl [--baseline other.jsonl]: a table of test / result / key fields, the list of registered encoders, a verdict line per PLAN stage-0 question (decode avc1? hvc1? encode avc1? hvc1? jpeg? heic write? aac?), and with --baseline what changed between two runs. Tolerates truncated last lines.
